newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE NOON SHARES MIXED AFTER VOLATILE SESSION.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE NOON SHARES MIXED AFTER VOLATILE SESSION.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed at noon on Friday after a volatile session with Singapore banks and selected blue chips going on a roller coaster ride.

Dealers said a Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) statement that it had no plans to ask banks to merge their foreign and local tranches stopped slides in foreign shares and gains in the local ones.

"The MAS statement looked initially very positive for banks but the statement also said it was up to the companies to decide for themselves. So I am telling my clients, foreign shares are looking cheap but there's still a downside risk," said a broker.
DBS shares ended the session down Singapore $0.10 to S$9.30 after hitting a new year high of S$10.20 earlier. Its foreign shares bounced off a low of S$16.60 to S$17.60, down 50 cents.
The foreign tranches of OUB and also OCBC rose 20 cents to S$8.65 and S$13.90 respectively.
Singapore Press local shares dropped 40 cents to S$12.90 while its foreign tranche fell S$1.20 to S$26.00.
The Straits Times Industrial Index stood at 1,937.33, down 15.91 points at 0430 GMT.
Total market volume was 87.26 million shares with 167 gainers against 128 losers.
